steps.text: Combine eggs, vinegar, mustard powder, and salt in the bowl of a food processor; pulse until blended. Pour oil in very slowly, with the processor running, until mayonnaise is smooth.

raw_recipe.headline: Whole Egg Mayonnaise
raw_recipe.description: This whole egg mayonnaise recipe uses whole eggs instead of just the yolks. The yolks act as an emulsifier, and the whites makes the mayo nice and fluffy.
raw_recipe.name: Whole Egg Mayonnaise

recipeInstructions.text: Combine eggs, vinegar, mustard powder, and salt in the bowl of a food processor; pulse until blended. Pour oil in very slowly, with the processor running, until mayonnaise is smooth.

review.reviewBody:
TWO SECRETS: To make mayonnaise come out with the right consistency, (and thus creamy taste), you MUST start with a very, very dry blender, and you must pour the oil in excruciatingly slowly. Do these two things, and you will never, ever buy store-bought mayonnaise again!

"Miracle Whip", add 1 to 2 Tbsp. sugar. (I don't do this, as I make my own mayonnaise for health reasons, as follows...)

HEART HEALTHY VERSION: use extra-virgin olive oil (organic if you can find it), and organic, free-range eggs.

More Tips: 1. You *must* have all ingredients at room temperature; 2. Use an immersion (stick-type) blender, if you have one. I have used my trusty Bamix since 1986 with outstanding results on this and many other recipes; 3. Be sure that the egg is the first ingredient added, followed by the vinegar (I use 1/2 red cider vinegar & 1/2 lemon juice), seasoning (I use 1/4 tsp to 1 C canola oil and the same amount of dry mustard as my mustard of choice), into a tall, narrow plastic cup (Halve the recipe for this method). Hold the blade on the bottom of the cup, turn it on to the fast speed for 20 seconds then move up & down slowly until completely mixed. Takes less than a minute, start to finish for delicious, homemade mayo! Other tips: Add finely minced chives, basil, cilantro, etc., or paprika or other spices ~ be inventive and enjoy. * * * This recipe tastes even better than Best Foods/Hellmann's mayo. We never have to buy pricey mayo. Once you try it, you may feel the same.

As long as you keep to the proportions of one egg to one cup oil to 1 tbsp acid and a little dollop of any kind of mustard and a taste of salt, you've got mayonnaise! I find that the easiest method for mixing this up is to put the egg in a widemouth jar first followed by all the other ingredients with the oil on top (avocado is nice) put an immersion blender in the bottom start it and gradually lift it to the top. The mixing container then becomes the storage container, much less hassle than trying to get all your mayonnaise out of a food processor. Just don't lick the beater! I make a half batch of this every time I need mayo. I haven't bought any for over 6 months.

Fantastic recipe! The perfect mayo for any recipe or sandwich. I will make this again. I used 3 eggs and a little extra mustard powder, a little more salt, a little agave because I like mayo to be slightly sweet, and I substituted fresh lemon juice for vinegar. Made for very tasty lobster rolls. I combined the ingredients in a mini food processor then added the oil VERY VERY slowly using a submersion blender. It was quick, easy, and a great-tasting mayo. Loved using the whole eggs.

As others have noted, it's faster if you use a stick blender and a tall, narrow container — you can use the jar you will store it in if it has a mouth wide enough to accept your blender's blade housing. You can add all the ingredients at once (eggs first, oil last), then pulse the stick blender for about 20 seconds, then run it constantly while moving it up and down. I find I get a thicker mayonnaise if I use three whole eggs and cut the oil to 1.5 cups. Cutting it to 1 cup should make it even thicker (and would probably work with two eggs as well). I accidentally doubled the amount of salt and dry mustard on the last batch I made — the taste was the same. This has become my go-to mayonnaise recipe. I haven't bought a jar of the stuff in more than a year!

I make a half recipe at a time (because we are empty nesters and don't use a lot of mayo!) and use my trusty stick blender. Put all ingredients in a wide mouth Mason jar; place the blender at the bottom of the jar and turn on, after it begins to emulsify, slowly raise stick blender until all is fully incorporated. I've also used lemon juice in place of the vinegar. Easy peasy, quick and easy! Why buy mayo at the store?

no more store bought mayo for this family! the immersion blender and a wide mouth quart sized Mason jar is the key to making this as easy and mess free as possible. 
eggs in the bottom, everything else on top, oil last. I have made it twice. the first time using half lemon juice, half apple cider vinegar. the 2nd time 2 tbsp of red wine vinegar. vegetable oil each time. both were amazing. I am going to keep trying different spice and acid variations for variety. this mayo made the shrimp salad from this site even tastier. 
starting at the bottom and blending up worked so quickly.

My first attempt at making mayo using this recipe failed as I poured the oil too fast. For my second attempt, I cut the recipe in half (so I didn't feel like I was wasting anything should it fail again). I also added a little bit of lemon juice. I at first thought I poured the oil too fast again so I prayed that it would thicken this time, and it did! I figured out I need to pour the oil at about 1/16-1/8 c. at a time. I'm going to make a full batch in a few days and test my theory. My husband said it'd take some getting used to but it didn't taste bad; I second it and say thanks for the recipe!

Edit 21 Apr. 20: I made a full batch making sure I poured the oil per the above rate and it worked out. I then employed an ingenious tip: Turn the blender at a 45° angle, unscrew the blender blades, and carefully separate them from the blender. Quickly set the bottom of the blender on top of the mouth of the mayonnaise jar and scrape the mayonnaise from the blender into the mayonnaise jar. Wrap a clean paper towel, if necessary, around the neck of the jar and blender where the two meet so the mayo can slide/fall into the mayo jar.

I know this recipe has been around awhile but I wanted to add my own variation which has never failed me. I make a 1/2 recipe as it can't hang around in the fridge for weeks like store bought mayo. And I pasteurize the egg by placing it in a pan of water at 140 deg f for 3 minutes, then cool. Place all ingredients, at room temperature, in a quart wide mouth mason jar. Use an immersion blender, start at the bottom of the jar and slowly move up. By the time you reach the top, it's done - just as thick and creamy as can be. Sometimes I fold in finely chopped herbs after blending. Enjoy!

I see others in the comments mention it's too oily. KEEP BLENDING. I used a Ninja blender, pouring the oil in from the spout. It was oily until I stopped, scraped with a spatula, and kept blending. It incorporated the oil more and added more volume. And YES, the recipe is bland. Season your mayo to your taste. For me, the important thing is that it emulsified well and made a creamy mayo. You can even season it once done blending. Use common sense, people. Good BASE RECIPE

This is like the umpteenth time I have made this and made another double batch. 
This time I used the leftover soybean oil from a jar of Tuscan Garden's mild giardiniera. This yielded almost a half cup. to that I added two cups of canola oil and the rest was olive oil to reach 4 cups. After blending, I pulled a pint and then mixed in three tablespoons of Chef John's Sriracha Chili Paste recipe previously made with the rest. Good Stuff!
I used this recipe with hard boiled eggs and it came out great.
This recipe always turns out perfectly . I use a big Mason jar & my stick/immersion blender. I’ve used a variety of oils and prepared mustard instead of powder. Thanks for the recipe!!
Used my stick blender right in the jar I'll store it in. Very easy and quick.
I use virgin olive oil to make this.
Made this once already, tastes great, very simple to make. I am going to try something a little different the next time for fun.
This recipe for Mayo is outstanding! The fam really liked it!
Worth the effort = what effort? Easy, everyday ingredients that most people have, with amazing results. I will never buy another jar of anything. Thank you

Made this recipe, Just HALFED everything and it came out perfectly. .... Used Emerson blender on low, pour in oil slow and steady the enitre time. Use a container that's a little wider then the blender head. Came out perfectly 🥰 I'm NEVER buying store mayonnaise again. Home made from now on. 🙌
Are we sure 2 cups of oil? Liquid mayonnaise….yuck
